writer.title: Private evidence needs permission
writer.draft_markdown:
# Private evidence needs permission

A private note should not become a public first-person scene merely because it would make the prose vivid. The source can be held for an owner decision, while the draft stays honest about what is not cleared. This bounded account names the evidence, keeps the audience aware of the approval boundary, and avoids turning a sensitive sentence into a public claim before the owner decides whether its use is appropriate. It also explains that an approved planning note can provide public context without transferring a restricted quote into the public story. The distinction protects the source, gives the editor a clear next decision, and keeps the draft useful while the owner reviews the proposed wording.
